decisions.reason: The public View and its initializer/body are implemented in the declared production Swift file; body constructs its private production content.
The content receives the supplied tour, renders tour.title and tour.language/downloadSizeMB and enumerates tour.chapters; status derives from the supplied model and local state.
The private production content owns chaptersOpen as @State initialized false.
The private production content owns wifiOnly as @State initialized true.
The private production content owns requested as @State initialized false.
The production public View keys its own content by tour.id; new identity recreates chaptersOpen at false.
The production public View keys its own content by tour.id; new identity recreates wifiOnly at true.
The production public View keys its own content by tour.id; new identity recreates requested at false.
Identity reset is solely production .id(tour.id) plus initial @State values; the reset path calls no caller callback.
Disclosure uses SwiftUI Button(action:) and the actual native button receives its identifier.
Choice uses SwiftUI Button(action:) and the actual native button receives its identifier.
Primary uses SwiftUI Button(action:) and the actual native button receives its identifier.
The choice adds native .isSelected accessibility traits conditionally from its actual wifiOnly state.
The choice uses .disabled(requested), as well as its action guard.
The primary uses .disabled(!canDownload), as well as its action guard.
Canvas uses accessibilityElement(children: .contain) around the production subtree, retaining descendant Button controls.
Surface uses accessibilityElement(children: .contain), with disclosure/choice/primary real Buttons inside.
Each required literal identifier occurs once on its real semantic carrier; section identifiers are generated once per enumerated caller index and kind.
The audio.status identifier is on the containing VStack after its status.fill background and actual band allocation.
audio.statusText is on the actual Text(status.label) child before band padding, without a fabricated proxy.
The complete file constructs stacks, text, rectangles and Buttons, and no ScrollView/List or other scrolling container.
The layout contains only meaningful blocks, ordinary padding and stack spacing; no fixed blank row manufactures scroll length.
ForEach enumerates tour.chapters directly; each iteration renders its chapter title then body in caller array order.
The complete file contains no observer imports, scenario/fixture selectors, fixture IDs or expected-value branches; only general model/state logic.
The enabled guarded primary callback calls onDownload(tour.id, wifiOnly) using the current content model.
The only business callback invocations are inside guarded choice and primary Button actions; initialization, rendering, disclosure and reset do not call them.
Disclosure action only toggles chaptersOpen, with no caller callback.
Primary has native disabled state and guards canDownload before its sole callback invocation.
Choice has native disabled state and guards !requested before mutation/callback.
No finite line cap is configured on the relevant Text nodes; the surface applies lineLimit(nil), with vertically growing Text allocations.
The primary Text label explicitly fills maxWidth infinity and then height 56 before background and content shape.
Rectangle contentShape is attached after the primary label full-width/56-height allocation and its background. This is construction evidence only.
The canvas is a noninteractive VStack with contain semantics and identifier; it declares no activation action or interactive role.
The surface is a noninteractive VStack semantic container; only its descendant Buttons activate.
The ink is a labelled Rectangle with identifier and no button trait, gesture or action.
canDownload is exactly the conjunction of sufficient storage, not metered-plus-wifiOnly, and not requested.
The status branches test insufficient storage, requested, metered plus wifiOnly, then ready in exactly that order.
The successful choice action guards !requested then invokes wifiOnly.toggle().
The callback is passed wifiOnly after toggle, so forwards the resulting preference.
The successful choice action has exactly one onWifiOnlyChange invocation and no loop or second branch.
After the eligibility guard, primary sets requested = true.
The successful primary action contains one onDownload call after setting requested, with no loop or second call.
Primary forwards the current wifiOnly value directly to onDownload.
Whole Int values are supplied in the model and compared directly; the complete file imports only SwiftUI and makes no disk-capacity query.
The complete component only records local requested state and emits a callback; no networking, file transfer, audio fetch or download exists.
The exact public stored String values, Equatable/Identifiable conformances and public initializer contract are present.
All exact public stored values/types, Equatable/Identifiable conformances and the public initializer parameter contract are present.
The public View, exact public initializer with escaping callbacks, and public body getter match the declaration contract.

The full production file uses SwiftUI APIs available by iOS 14: foundational Views/controls/modifiers, @State, ForEach, .id, custom ButtonStyle and accessibility traits. It introduces no unguarded post-iOS-14 API. This is source availability review, not older-OS launch or packaging proof.
The bridge only decodes the caller model and constructs the declared production component; it builds no substitute UI.
The complete thin bridge declares no local component business state or persistent local mutable preference.
The bridge calls the production component directly and adds no .id or key identity-reset wrapper.
The current fixture argument is decoded field-for-field into production models, including chapter order.
The actual production callbacks are forwarded to onEvent using supplied callback ID/preference values; no expected callbacks are fabricated.
The declared models and real @Composable production function are defined in the exact Kotlin production file and package.
The function consumes the supplied tour, renders title/language/downloadSizeMB and caller chapters, with general state/model-derived status.
Production owns chaptersOpen in remember(tour.id) initialized false.
Production owns wifiOnly in remember(tour.id) initialized true.
Production owns requested in remember(tour.id) initialized false.
remember is keyed by tour.id, so a changed caller identity reinitializes disclosure false.
remember is keyed by tour.id, so a changed caller identity reinitializes wifiOnly true.
remember is keyed by tour.id, so a changed caller identity reinitializes requested false.
The identity-keyed state initializers and derived guards contain no caller callback invocation.
Disclosure uses Material3 TextButton, a real Compose native Button semantic control.
Choice uses Material3 TextButton and puts its actual identifier and selected semantics on that control.
Primary uses Material3 Button, with enabled and identifier on the real control.
Choice sets semantics selected = wifiOnly directly from its current local state.
Choice sets the actual TextButton enabled argument to !requested.
Primary sets the actual Button enabled argument to canDownload.
Canvas uses semantics(mergeDescendants = false), with independently tagged controls in the contained production layout.
Surface uses semantics(mergeDescendants = false), preserving independently tagged descendant controls.
Each declared literal testTag is attached once to its real node. Section heading/body tags use each caller index once in the single forEachIndexed.
audio.status tags the actual painted Box bearing status.fill before internal padding; there is no proxy allocation.
audio.statusText tags the actual Text(status.label) child allocation.
The complete file constructs Columns, Box/Row, Text and native Buttons; no scrolling container or scroll modifier is introduced.
The only Spacer is the 8dp horizontal space between checkbox and label; layout has no blank fixed-height rows manufacturing scrolling.
forEachIndexed directly enumerates tour.chapters, rendering each chapter title then body in caller order.
The complete file contains no observer/scenario/fixture-specific selectors, IDs or expected-result comparisons; only general supplied-model/state logic.
The guarded actual primary action directly passes current tour.id to onDownload.
The only caller callback invocations occur in enabled choice/primary onClick lambdas, each with its own guard; render/reset/disclosure invoke none.
Disclosure onClick only flips chaptersOpen; no caller callback occurs.
The real Button enabled gate and repeated eligibility check protect the sole download callback.
The native enabled gate and !requested guard protect the sole choice callback.
No Text node in any required role sets maxLines to a finite value; all retain Compose Text uncapped defaults.
The real Button fills width at height 56dp; its label Box fills max size and Text fills width, constructing the full declared allocation.
The Button uses RectangleShape on its full-width/56dp allocation, with no border/elevation and zero contentPadding; its label Box fills that same rectangle. This does not prove physical hit bounds.
Canvas is a tagged nonmerging Column with no clickable modifier, activation action or interactive role.
Surface is a tagged nonmerging Column with no activation action or interactive role.
Ink is a solid tagged Box with only a contentDescription; no click action or interactive role is set.
canDownload exactly compares sufficient storage, rejects metered-plus-wifiOnly and rejects requested.
The when branches follow insufficient storage, requested, metered-plus-wifiOnly, then ready.
Under !requested the successful choice action sets wifiOnly = !wifiOnly.
onWifiOnlyChange receives wifiOnly after it has been inverted.
The successful guarded choice action invokes onWifiOnlyChange exactly once, with no loop or extra call.
The successful eligible primary branch changes requested to true before its callback.
The eligible primary branch contains exactly one onDownload invocation; repeated calls are guarded by requested.
onDownload is passed the current wifiOnly local Boolean directly.
The complete file takes Int availableMB/downloadSizeMB from the caller and compares them; it calls no disk-capacity API.
The complete component records state and invokes a callback only; no audio/network/file fetch or transfer exists.
The data class has exactly the declared String val properties and constructor parameter names/order.
The data class has the declared seven val model properties, exact types and parameter order.
The exact @Composable function parameters/callback types and modifier: Modifier = Modifier default are present.
The bridge only decodes the caller model and constructs the declared production component; it builds no substitute UI.
The complete thin bridge declares no local component business state or persistent local mutable preference.
The bridge calls the production component directly and adds no .id or key identity-reset wrapper.
The current fixture argument is decoded field-for-field into production models, including chapter order.
The actual production callbacks are forwarded to onEvent using supplied callback ID/preference values; no expected callbacks are fabricated.
